title: Block both lenses for edging, each block 8 mm temporal of the optical centre
instruction: Block both lenses for edging at the frame's boxing centre. For this job (eye size 54 mm, bridge 20 mm, PD 58 mm) that is (54 + 20 - 58) / 2 = 8 mm temporal of the optical centre. On each lens, set one blue block flat with its centre 8 mm from the centre of the black dot (the optical centre) along the black ink line, on the side away from the small black square (the nasal mark), with the block's long side along the line. Then let go of both blocks.
context: Ophthalmic laboratory technicians (O*NET 51-9083.00) lay out and block every lens before edging. A lensmeter marks the optical centre (OC) and the 180 line; then a block, the edger's chuck, is stuck on the lens. Many labs block at the frame's boxing centre, (A + DBL - PD) / 2 temporal of the OC, so the edger needs no decentration entered, with the block's flat along the 180 line, or the edged shape, and a cylinder's axis with it, comes out turned. ANSI Z80.1 allows about 0.67 prism dioptres of horizontal imbalance (about 2.5 mm of PD error at low powers) and +-2 deg of axis on cylinders over 1.50 D; by Prentice's rule a -4.00 D lens 8 mm off carries 3.2 prism dioptres. A narrow PD in a wide frame blocked on the OC out of habit is the classic remake. The task catches blocking on the OC (8 mm off), on the nasal side (16 mm off) or unturned (25 or 30 deg off); the two lenses' temporal sides mirror each other across the pair.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, heights are above the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Headings are angles seen from above, from +x toward +y. Everything is fixed except the two blocks. (1) Two layout pads (a blocker's lens tables): white acrylic plates 120 x 120 x 8 mm, sides along x and y, fixed, centred at x 30.0 cm, y +24.0 cm (left) and x 30.0 cm, y -24.0 cm (right). (2) Two uncut spectacle lenses: CR-39 discs 70 mm across and 4 mm thick with a pale blue tint, fixed flat at the centre of each pad (bottom 8 mm, top 12.0 mm above the table), as a blocker's lens holder holds them. (3) Lensmeter marks on each lens, black ink inlays 0.4 mm thick standing 0.1 mm proud of the lens top: an 8 mm dot at the lens's centre, the optical centre (OC); a straight 180 line 60 mm long and 4 mm wide centred on the OC; and a 10 x 10 mm nasal square, sides along the line, centred on the line 26 mm from the OC (it spans 21 to 31 mm), toward the midline. Left lens: the line runs at heading 115 degrees (turned 25 degrees anticlockwise from y), the square centred at x 31.10 cm, y +21.64 cm. Right lens: the line runs at heading 60 degrees (turned 30 degrees clockwise from y), the square centred at x 31.30 cm, y -21.75 cm. So each lens's temporal side, away from its square, points away from the midline, and the point 8 mm temporal of the OC along the line is at x 29.66 cm, y +24.73 cm (left) and x 29.60 cm, y -24.69 cm (right). (4) Two edger blocks, loose: blue acetal (POM) boxes 18 x 24 x 16 mm, 10 g each, standing on an 18 x 24 mm face on the table with the 24 mm side along y, centred at x 16.0 cm, y +31.0 cm (left) and x 16.0 cm, y -31.0 cm (right). The 24 mm side stands for a real block's locating flat. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored at the last step from the two blocks' poses and the two grippers' tool points (TCP, 13 mm above the finger tips) and openings. The same rule applies to each lens. A block is on a lens when its centre, seen from above, is within 35 mm of that lens's OC and less than 60 mm above the lens top. A lens is blocked when all of these hold: (a) exactly one block is on it; (b) the block is flat: its 16 mm axis within 3 degrees of vertical (either 18 x 24 mm face down); (c) seated: its lowest corner within 2 mm of the lens top; (d) still: over the last 0.5 s its centre moved at most 2 mm in all and it turned at most 2 degrees in all; (e) let go: no gripper whose TCP is within 40 mm of the block's centre is less than half open (pads under 47 mm apart); at a step when the grippers cannot be read, no lens counts as let go. d is the horizontal distance from the block's centre to the lens's target, the point 8 mm from the OC along the ink line on the side away from the nasal square; a is the angle seen from above between the block's 24 mm side and the line (0 to 90 degrees; a block turned half a turn or upside down is the same block). Each lens scores 0.5 if blocked with d at most 2 mm and a at most 3 degrees; otherwise 0.25 if blocked with d at most 3 mm and a at most 6 degrees; otherwise 0 (no block, two blocks, tilted, on its side, not seated, still moving, still held, or further off). The score is the left lens's plus the right lens's. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0; each lens is in exactly one state, so every outcome maps to exactly one score. The start scores 0. Success (1.0) ends the trial once it has held for 1 s; it cannot begin before both blocks are let go. Otherwise the last step is scored. Reference cases: a block centred on the OC is 8 mm off (0); on the nasal side, 16 mm off (0); not turned, 25 degrees (left) or 30 degrees (right) off (0); set 8 mm straight out along y instead of along the line, and turned, 3.5 mm off on the left lens and 4.1 mm off on the right (0 on both); measured 8 mm from the dot's edge instead of its centre, 4 mm off (0). Either block may go on either lens. In a real trial, take a top photo with the grippers clear: a correct block hides the dot, but the 60 mm line is centred on the OC, so its two visible ends locate the OC and the target; measure d with a ruler and a with a protractor against the line, check flatness with a square and seating with a 2 mm feeler gauge, and judge stillness and let-go from the video's last second.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, one friction. Flat fixed discs stand in for meniscus lenses. Real blocks are round, with a flat and a sticky pad; ours are boxes that may slide. A lensmeter prints three dots; we ink the line through them, enlarged for the cameras. A blocker turns the lens to its crosshair; here the lens is fixed and the block turned. No vertical decentration. Bands (2 mm, 3 degrees) are looser than a lab's (1 mm, 2 degrees): simulated arms place to 1 to 3 mm. Two pads let both arms work.
reset_notes: Stand both blocks back on the table on an 18 x 24 mm face with the 24 mm side along y, centred at x 16.0 cm, y +31.0 cm and x 16.0 cm, y -31.0 cm. The pads and lenses stay taped down; check that the marks are intact. Nothing is consumed (a real block's adhesive pad would be replaced each time).
